description: Ticketing systems and CMDB — incident trends, SLA compliance, MTTR, and change management correlation.
name: Service Management & ITSM
quickFacts: Use Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow or REST API integration to pull ticket and CMDB data.

useCases.title: Incident Volume Trending
useCases.value: Incident trends reveal infrastructure stability, staffing needs, and the effectiveness of problem management.

useCases.title: SLA Compliance Monitoring
useCases.value: SLA breaches affect customer satisfaction and contractual obligations. Real-time monitoring enables intervention before breaches occur.

useCases.title: MTTR by Category
useCases.value: MTTR per category identifies where process improvements or automation would have the greatest impact.

useCases.title: Change Success Rate
useCases.value: Failed changes are the leading cause of incidents. Tracking success rate drives improvement in change management practices.

useCases.title: Change Collision Detection
useCases.value: Overlapping changes on related systems increase outage risk. Detection enables coordination and conflict resolution.

useCases.title: Problem Trending
useCases.value: Identifying recurring incident patterns that should become problems drives root cause resolution and reduces incident volume.

useCases.title: Ticket Reassignment Rate
useCases.value: High reassignment rates indicate poor routing or skills gaps. Reduction improves MTTR and customer satisfaction.

useCases.title: Aging Ticket Alerts
useCases.value: Aging tickets indicate stuck processes or forgotten issues. Alerts ensure nothing falls through the cracks.

useCases.title: Change-Incident Correlation
useCases.value: Correlating incidents with recent changes is the fastest path to root cause. Automated correlation accelerates MTTR.

useCases.title: Service Request Fulfillment Time
useCases.value: Fulfillment time metrics drive service catalog optimization and customer satisfaction. Slow fulfillment reduces adoption.

useCases.title: Problem Ticket Reopening Rate
useCases.value: Tickets closed then reopened indicate poor resolution quality, incomplete fixes, or inadequate testing. Tracking reopening rate drives resolution discipline and reduces repeat work.

useCases.title: Incident Priority Distribution Trending
useCases.value: Are P1/P2 incidents increasing? Trend analysis for management reporting reveals workload shifts, infrastructure degradation, or seasonal patterns. Supports staffing and capacity planning.

useCases.title: On-Call Escalation Frequency
useCases.value: Rising escalation rate indicates team capacity or knowledge gaps. Unacknowledged or escalated incidents signal burnout risk and process bottlenecks. Supports on-call rotation tuning and training.

useCases.title: SLA Breach Prediction
useCases.value: Predicting tickets likely to breach SLA before the deadline enables proactive reassignment, escalation, and automation — reducing contractual exposure and customer impact.

useCases.title: Incident Reassignment Frequency
useCases.value: Trending reassignment frequency (per period and per group) exposes routing quality, skills gaps, and noisy categories — complementing per-ticket reassignment counts.

useCases.title: Ticket Aging by Priority
useCases.value: Distribution of open ticket age by priority highlights backlog imbalance (e.g., many old P3s) and supports capacity and escalation decisions.

useCases.title: Auto-Close Compliance
useCases.value: Tracks incidents resolved by auto-close rules vs manual closure; excess auto-close may indicate poor engagement or policy gaming; too few may mean workflows are not firing.

useCases.title: Recurring Incident Detection
useCases.value: Clusters of similar incidents within a short window signal candidates for problem records, known-error articles, or permanent fixes.

useCases.title: Problem Management Root Cause Linking
useCases.value: Ensures resolved incidents are tied to problem records with root cause when repeat patterns exist — closing the loop for ITIL problem management.

useCases.title: Major Incident Post-Mortem Compliance
useCases.value: Verifies that major incidents have completed post-mortems within policy — extending generic PIR tracking with explicit compliance scoring for Sev1 programs.

useCases.title: War Room Activation Tracking
useCases.value: Tracks when bridge/war-room workflows activate (chat, conference bridges, tags) for major incidents — supporting governance and after-action metrics.

useCases.title: Escalation Path Audit
useCases.value: Audits whether incidents followed the documented escalation chain (L1→L2→vendor) for compliance and training.

useCases.title: Service Request Fulfillment Rate
useCases.value: Percentage of catalog requests fulfilled successfully within the reporting period — distinct from average fulfillment time (UC-16.1.10).

useCases.title: ServiceNow Bidirectional Incident Sync
useCases.value: Bidirectional sync between ITSI episodes and ServiceNow incidents eliminates manual ticket creation and ensures incident status is consistent across platforms.

useCases.title: First Response Time vs SLA Target
useCases.value: First response time is a leading indicator of resolution SLA performance; trending FRT against targets aligns the service desk with ITIL service level practices and highlights queue starvation before…

useCases.title: Catalog Request Item Backlog and WIP
useCases.value: A growing backlog of open request items signals fulfillment bottlenecks or catalog misconfiguration; monitoring WIP by catalog item supports request fulfilment SLAs and ITIL service request lifecycle…

useCases.title: On-Hold Time Impact on Resolution SLA
useCases.value: Excessive on-hold time often explains resolution SLA misses without reflecting true work effort; measuring hold hours by category supports ITIL incident lifecycle controls and customer communication…

useCases.title: CMDB Data Quality Score
useCases.value: Poor CMDB data quality undermines all ITSM processes. Scoring and trending drives data quality improvement initiatives.

useCases.title: CI Discovery Reconciliation
useCases.value: CIs in the network but not in the CMDB are unmanaged risks. Reconciliation ensures CMDB completeness.

useCases.title: Orphaned CI Detection
useCases.value: CIs without owners or service mappings aren't managed during incidents, creating accountability gaps and shadow infrastructure.

useCases.title: Relationship Integrity Check
useCases.value: Accurate CI relationships enable impact analysis during incidents. Incomplete relationships undermine service mapping.

useCases.title: CMDB Change Audit
useCases.value: Tracking all CI attribute changes supports compliance auditing and helps detect unauthorized configuration changes.

useCases.title: CI Relationship Drift
useCases.value: Detects when CI relationships change unexpectedly versus a baseline — supporting impact analysis integrity and unauthorized dependency changes.

useCases.title: Asset Discovery Reconciliation
useCases.value: Reconciles discovery source of truth against CMDB for asset inventory — variance by source, age, and confidence.

useCases.title: End-of-Life Hardware Tracking
useCases.value: Surfaces CIs past vendor EOS/EOL dates for refresh planning and security risk reduction.

useCases.title: CMDB Accuracy Scoring
useCases.value: Scores accuracy by sampling validation (discovery match, pingable, owner confirmed) — complements completeness-focused quality scores.

useCases.title: Undocumented Server Detection
useCases.value: Finds servers visible to monitoring or AD but missing from CMDB — classic gap for incident routing and security scope.

useCases.title: Software Asset Management Compliance
useCases.value: Measures install counts vs license entitlements for major publishers — SAM compliance for audits.

useCases.title: Hardware Warranty Expiry
useCases.value: Tracks warranty end dates for hardware CIs to avoid unsupported break-fix gaps and budget surprises.

useCases.title: CI Lifecycle Management
useCases.value: Monitors CI lifecycle state transitions (ordered → received → in production → retired) for stuck states and policy compliance.

useCases.title: Asset Decommission Verification
useCases.value: Confirms decommissioned servers no longer appear in monitoring, AD, or hypervisor inventory — reducing zombie assets and license bleed.

useCases.title: Stale CI Discovery Freshness
useCases.value: Operational CIs without recent discovery updates inflate false confidence during impact analysis; freshness trending supports CMDB governance and ITIL configuration management objectives.

useCases.title: Duplicate CI Name Detection
useCases.value: Duplicate names break joins between incidents, changes, and monitoring; detecting duplicates early restores CMDB accuracy and reduces routing errors across ITSM processes.

useCases.title: Application CI Business Service Coverage
useCases.value: Applications without a business service mapping weaken BIA-driven prioritization and incident impact statements; coverage metrics align the CMDB with ITIL service asset and configuration practices.

useCases.title: CMDB Mandatory Attribute Completeness by Class
useCases.value: Class-specific mandatory fields (owner, environment, support group) drive automation and reporting; completeness scoring by `ci_class` gives CMDB stewards actionable ITIL-aligned quality targets.

useCases.title: Cross-Service Business Process Health Score
useCases.value: Individual component alerts do not communicate business impact. A BPI model aggregates the health of all components that together constitute a business capability (e.g., "Order Processing = web tier…

useCases.title: Infrastructure Service Availability Heatmap
useCases.value: Provides a Nagios-style tactical overview — at a glance, which hosts and services have been available vs down, when, and for how long. Operations teams use this for SLA evidence, post-incident review…

useCases.title: First Contact Resolution Rate by Group
useCases.value: FCR indicates support efficiency and customer satisfaction. Tracking by group and category supports staffing and process improvement.

useCases.title: Escalation and Handoff Latency
useCases.value: Long escalation or handoff times delay resolution. Monitoring handoff duration supports SLA and identifies bottlenecks.

useCases.title: Knowledge Article Usage and Gap Detection
useCases.value: Low article use or repeated incidents without matching KB may indicate content gaps. Analytics support knowledge management and deflection.

useCases.title: Major Incident and Post-Mortem Tracking
useCases.value: Tracking major incidents and post-mortem completion ensures learning and accountability. Supports compliance and continuous improvement.

useCases.title: Request Fulfillment and Approval Cycle Time
useCases.value: Long approval or fulfillment times delay service delivery. Monitoring cycle time supports process optimization and SLA for requests.

useCases.title: Knowledge Article Usage vs. Ticket Volume
useCases.value: Self-service effectiveness measurement; are KB articles deflecting tickets? Correlating article views with ticket creation reveals deflection ROI and content gaps.

useCases.title: Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) per CI
useCases.value: Reliability trending per configuration item for replacement planning. CIs with declining MTBF indicate aging hardware or recurring issues; supports proactive replacement and warranty decisions.

useCases.title: Business Service Availability (Composite SLA)
useCases.value: Rolls up component availability into a single business-service SLA percentage (weighted or “all essential up”) for customer-facing reporting — beyond host-level heatmaps.

useCases.title: Batch Job Schedule Compliance
useCases.value: Verifies scheduled batch jobs (ETL, billing, backups) started and finished within expected windows — catching silent scheduler failures before downstream SLAs break.

useCases.title: Control-M Job Monitoring
useCases.value: Batch job success/failure and SLA compliance are critical for data pipelines and scheduled workloads. Failed or late jobs can cascade to downstream systems and reporting.

useCases.title: Service Request Item Fulfillment Cycle Time
useCases.value: Cycle time for catalog line items reflects fulfillment team capacity and automation maturity; tracking medians by item aligns operations with ITIL request fulfilment metrics and customer-facing SLAs.

useCases.title: Priority 1–2 First-Assignment Latency
useCases.value: Time-to-first-assignment for urgent incidents measures triage discipline and major-incident readiness; reducing latency supports ITIL event-to-incident handling and response SLA guardrails.

useCases.title: Open Problem Record Aging
useCases.value: Aging open problems indicate stalled root-cause work and undermine permanent corrective actions; backlog visibility strengthens ITIL problem management cadence with incident and change stakeholders.

useCases.title: Knowledge Article Effectiveness on Incidents
useCases.value: Comparing incidents that reference knowledge articles versus those that do not shows whether the knowledge base reduces handle time and repeat contacts—core ITIL knowledge management feedback.

useCases.title: Unauthorized Change Detection
useCases.value: Changes executed without approval or outside policy create audit exposure and outage risk; detecting them early supports SOC-2/ITIL controls and rapid rollback decisions.

useCases.title: Change Window Compliance Monitoring
useCases.value: Work performed outside agreed maintenance windows disrupts users and breaks SLAs; measuring compliance enforces scheduling discipline and supports customer communication.

useCases.title: Failed Change Correlation with Incident Spikes
useCases.value: Linking unsuccessful changes to incident volume proves root cause for major reviews and helps tighten testing or rollback criteria for similar changes.

useCases.title: Release Deployment Success Rate Tracking
useCases.value: Release success rate summarizes delivery health; sustained drops signal quality gaps in testing, automation, or release windows.

useCases.title: Emergency Change Frequency Monitoring
useCases.value: Chronic reliance on emergency changes indicates planning gaps or unstable platforms; trending frequency guides process improvement and capacity investments.

useCases.title: Change Advisory Board (CAB) Approval Compliance
useCases.value: CAB sign-off for high-risk changes is a control point; measuring compliance before implementation reduces unauthorized production risk.

useCases.title: Post-Implementation Review (PIR) Completion Tracking
useCases.value: PIRs capture lessons from major incidents and failed changes; tracking completion closes the feedback loop and satisfies audit expectations after Sev1 events.

useCases.title: Change Risk Assessment Accuracy
useCases.value: If “low risk” changes often fail or drive incidents, the risk model is miscalibrated; analytics improve scoring and reduce surprise outages.

useCases.title: Change Backout and Rollback Rate
useCases.value: Backouts indicate customer-impacting defects or planning gaps; trending rollback rates informs ITIL change evaluation and release quality gates before the next deployment wave.

useCases.title: Change Implementation Duration vs Plan
useCases.value: Overruns against the approved implementation window increase collision risk and customer impact; comparing actual versus planned duration reinforces ITIL change scheduling and CAB commitments.

useCases.title: Same-CI Concurrent Scheduled Changes
useCases.value: Multiple overlapping implementations against one CI amplify outage risk; detecting concurrent schedules supports ITIL change coordination and collision analysis ahead of CAB approval.

useCases.title: Standard Change Volume and Mix Guardrail
useCases.value: A sudden spike in standard changes may indicate bypassing normal scrutiny; monitoring volume and mix supports ITIL delegated authority models without eroding risk controls.

useCases.title: Ticket Backlog Aging Trending
useCases.value: Watching how open work ages shows whether queues are draining or stagnating; growth in older buckets signals staffing, tooling, or upstream failure demand that will eventually breach customer expecta…

useCases.title: Change Success Rate Trending
useCases.value: A falling change success rate warns that testing, communication, or risk scoring is degrading before major outages; trending by week ties process fixes to measurable improvement.

useCases.title: Knowledge Article Deflection Rate Trending
useCases.value: Deflection measures whether self-service content reduces human-handled tickets; sustained improvement validates knowledge investment and lowers support cost.

useCases.title: MTTR by Priority Trending
useCases.value: Priority-weighted resolution time shows whether urgent work truly gets faster attention; quarterly trends highlight chronic bottlenecks for P1/P2 paths.

useCases.title: Escalation Rate Trending
useCases.value: Escalations consume senior time and often reflect unclear front-line tooling; a rising share of escalated incidents points to training gaps, bad routing, or unstable services.

useCases.title: First Response SLA Compliance Trending
useCases.value: Trending first-response compliance shows whether the desk keeps pace with contractual response SLAs before resolution work begins; sustained dips trigger ITIL service level review and staffing adjust…

useCases.title: Incident Channel Mix Trending
useCases.value: Channel mix (portal, phone, chat, email) influences staffing models and self-service ROI; trending aligns workforce management with ITIL service desk strategy and digital adoption goals.

useCases.title: Open Incident WIP Trending by Priority
useCases.value: Work-in-progress counts by priority show whether urgent queues are accumulating independent of new volume; trending WIP supports ITIL capacity management for the service desk and early escalation to…
